We need to isolate $a.$ To do this, we first add $2$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =-14ab-2 \\ 5+2 & =-14ab-2+2 \\ 7 & =-14ab\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $-14b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7 & =-14ab \\ \frac{7}{-14b} & =\frac{-14ab}{-14b} \\ \frac{7}{-14b} & =\frac{\cancel{-14b}a}{\cancel{-14b}} \\ -\frac{7}{14b} & =a\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{7}{7\cdot 2b} & =a \\ -\frac{\cancel{7}}{\cancel{7}\cdot 2b} & =a \\ -\frac{1}{2b} & =a \\ a & =-\frac{1}{2b}\end{aligned}
$$

Example: 
                    Solving Equations With Unknown Coefficients
canonical_examples.problem: Solve the equation $5ky-13=7$ for the variable $y.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $y.$ To do this, we first add $13$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5ky-13 & =7 \\ 5ky-13+13 & =7+13 \\ 5ky & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $5k\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5ky & =20 \\ \frac{5ky}{5k} & =\frac{20}{5k} \\ \frac{\cancel{5k}y}{\cancel{5k}} & =\frac{20}{5k} \\ y & =\frac{20}{5k}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can further simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{5\cdot 4}{5k} \\ y & =\frac{\cancel{5}\cdot 4}{\cancel{5}k} \\ y & =\frac{4}{k}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Solving Equations Containing Fractions
canonical_examples.problem: Solve the equation $\dfrac 34 kx + 9 = 2$ for the variable $x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $4$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}kx+9 & =2 \\ 4\cdot (\frac{3}{4}kx+9) & =4\cdot 2 \\ 3kx+36 & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to isolate $x.$ To do this, we first subtract $36$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}3kx+36 & =8 \\ 3kx+36-36 & =8-36 \\ 3kx & =-28\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $3k\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}3kx & =-28 \\ \frac{3kx}{3k} & =\frac{-28}{3k} \\ \frac{\cancel{3k}x}{\cancel{3k}} & =\frac{-28}{3k} \\ x & =-\frac{28}{3k}\end{aligned}
$$

Example: 
                    Solving Equations Using Cross Multiplication
canonical_examples.problem: Solve the equation $\dfrac{1}{3} = -\dfrac{ax}{5}$ for the variable $x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $x.$ To do this, we first cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} & =-\frac{ax}{5} \\ \frac{1}{3} & =\frac{-ax}{5} \\ 5\cdot 1 & =3\cdot (-ax) \\ 5 & =-3ax\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $-3a\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =-3ax \\ \frac{5}{-3a} & =\frac{-3ax}{-3a} \\ \frac{5}{-3a} & =\frac{\cancel{-3a}x}{\cancel{-3a}} \\ -\frac{5}{3a} & =x \\ x & =-\frac{5}{3a}\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Consider the following equation:

$$
2{\color{red}m}{\color{blue}t} = 1
$$

Notice that this equation has two variables, ${\color{red}m}$ and ${\color{blue}t}.$ Suppose we want to solve the equation for the variable ${\color{blue}t}.$

To isolate ${\color{blue}t},$ we apply the multiplication principle and divide both sides of the equation by $2{\color{red}m},$ treating ${\color{red}m}$ as though it were a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}2mt & =1 \\ \frac{2mt}{2m} & =\frac{1}{2m} \\ \frac{\cancel{2m}t}{\cancel{2m}} & =\frac{1}{2m} \\ t & =\frac{1}{2m}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we'll take a look at an example where we need to apply both the addition and multiplication principles.
